newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African bomb suspect arrested on Namibian border.
newsitem.headline: S.African bomb suspect arrested on Namibian border.

text.p: A suspect in a Christmas Eve bomb attack that killed four people in a small South African farming town has been arrested on the Namibian border, state radio reported on Saturday.

Namibian authorities deported Jan van der Westhuizen after discovering he was an illegal alien, the radio reported. He was then arrested by police on the South African side of the border at Ariamsvlei.
He will appear in court at Worcester -- site of the blasts -- on Monday. No other details were available.
Four other people have already been arrested in connection with the attack.

An adult and three children were killed and about 60 people wounded when twin pipe bombs exploded at a supermarket and pharmacy on December 24 in Worcester, 90 km (55 miles) northeast of Cape Town. Most of the casualties were blacks or mixed-race.

An unknown white right-wing group, the Boere Attack Troops (BAT), claimed responsibility for the blasts and demanded the release of right-wingers in jail, self-rule for Afrikaners, and a drastic drop in fuel prices.
